title: Kapiva vs. HK Vitals vs. HealthKart in India (2026): Labels, Lab Reports & Safe Buying
description: These are not direct substitutes: Kapiva sells Ayurvedic resins, HK Vitals sells daily nutraceuticals, and HealthKart is a multi-brand sports-nutrition marketplace. Compare label transparency, cost per serving and verification options — not headline discounts. No health or efficacy claims are made here.

forWho: Adults in India comparing an Ayurvedic resin, a daily collagen or a whey protein, and wanting to check label data and cost per serving before buying.
Shoppers who want to know which channels publish batch reports or authentication tools they can check themselves.
skipIf: Pregnant or lactating women, anyone under 18, and people with kidney, liver or endocrine conditions or on prescription medication — speak to a qualified doctor first.
Anyone seeking treatment or disease management. Dietary supplements do not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent disease, and this page makes no efficacy claims.

content_blocks.body: Pick by category, not by brand loyalty. Kapiva Himalayan Shilajit Resin 20g is ₹999 on the brand site with a 250mg serving (80 servings, ≈₹12.5 per serving) and the brand states NABL reports are available per pack. HK Vitals Skin Radiance Marine Collagen 200g is ₹909 with 5g collagen and 40mg vitamin C stated per serving (≈40 servings, ≈₹22.7 per serving) and is non-vegetarian (fish). MuscleBlaze Biozyme Performance Whey 1kg is listed at ₹3,999 with 25g protein per 36g scoop across 28 servings (≈₹142.8 per serving, ≈₹5.7 per gram of protein); the retailer states third-party certification, which you should verify on the exact batch. All figures were checked on 24 Nov 2026. Because these are different product categories, no single winner should be declared across all three; choose within the category that matches your buying goal.

content_blocks.heading: Out-of-the-Box Insider Reality (What Other Sites Won't Tell You)
items: These three products are not alternatives to each other. A resin, a collagen powder and a whey tub solve different purchase questions — compare within a category, not across it.
A 'clinically proven' line on a brand page is not evidence by itself. We do not repeat efficacy claims on this page because no named study is cited in the sources we reviewed.
Batch reports must match the batch code printed on your pack. A generic certificate from a different batch is not the same thing.
*Prices are snapshots from 24 Nov 2026 and change during sales. Cost per serving divides the reviewed price by the stated servings; it is arithmetic on published data, not a measured result.

We did not purchase, consume or independently lab-test any of these products. We make no medical claims. If you have a medical condition, are pregnant, or take medication, consult a qualified professional.

content_blocks.heading: 1. Label transparency — Winner: HK Vitals (5 g + 40 mg stated per serving)
paragraphs: Of the three official pages we reviewed, HK Vitals states the most specific per-serving numbers for its marine collagen: 5 g collagen and 40 mg vitamin C, with a 200 g jar. MuscleBlaze states 25 g protein per 36 g scoop across 28 servings. Kapiva states 60%+ fulvic acid but dosing is a 250 mg measure by spoon, so exact daily intake depends on how level the scoop is.

content_blocks.heading: 2. Cost per serving — Winner: Kapiva (≈₹12.5 per serving)
paragraphs: Dividing the reviewed price by stated servings gives ≈₹12.5 per Kapiva serving, ≈₹22.7 per HK Vitals serving and ≈₹142.8 per whey serving. These are not comparable benefits — they are different product categories — but the arithmetic stops a ₹999 jar from looking cheaper than it is without knowing the serving count.

content_blocks.heading: 3. Batch testing claims — Winner: whichever brand gives you a matching COA
paragraphs: Kapiva states NABL reports are available with every pack; HK Vitals states third-party testing; the MuscleBlaze retailer page names Informed Choice, Labdoor and Trustified checks. We have not verified any specific certificate. Ask for the report matching the batch code on your pack before you rely on it.

content_blocks.heading: 4. Allergens and dietary markers — Winner: no brand, check the label
paragraphs: HK Vitals collagen is explicitly non-vegetarian because it comes from fish. The whey carries a vegetarian dot but contains milk and soy. Kapiva's resin is labelled vegetarian and the brand says it is not for pregnant or lactating women and is for adults over 18. Read the back panel of the exact SKU rather than the front-of-pack claim.

content_blocks.heading: 5. Purchase channel — Winner: brand-direct where verification is supported
paragraphs: HealthKart describes an HK Verify scratch-code check on eligible products; brand-direct stores give you a clearer invoice and batch trail. Unknown marketplace resellers are where counterfeit and storage complaints concentrate. Keep the invoice and batch number for any return or quality question.

content_blocks.heading: What we verified, and what we did not
paragraphs: A 25 Nov 2026 evidence pass confirmed Kapiva Shilajit pricing across three listings: ₹988 on Amazon (sold by RK World Infocom), ₹999 direct from Kapiva, and ₹1,004 on PharmEasy. MRPs conflict across sources (₹1,199 on Amazon and the brand site vs ₹1,499 on PharmEasy), so verify the exact MRP at checkout. The HK Vitals and MuscleBlaze URLs in that pass returned no extractable SKU data; their figures on this page come from our earlier checks dated 24 Nov 2026. We did not purchase, consume, or commission laboratory testing on any product, make no health or efficacy claims, and could not open a batch-specific COA. Prices are dated snapshots and change during sales.

Use authentication checks where the product supports them.

items.q: Which should I buy: Kapiva, HK Vitals or a whey tub from HealthKart?
items.a: They are different categories. Kapiva Himalayan Shilajit Resin 20g is an Ayurvedic resin at ₹999 with 250 mg servings (≈₹12.5/serving). HK Vitals Marine Collagen 200g is a fish-derived daily supplement at ₹909 with 5 g collagen per serving (≈₹22.7/serving). MuscleBlaze Biozyme Whey 1kg is sports nutrition at ₹3,999 with 25 g protein per 36 g scoop (≈₹5.7 per gram of protein). Choose within your category and verify the label.

items.q: How do I check a batch lab report?
items.a: Find the batch code printed on your pack, then ask the brand for the certificate of analysis matching that code. A generic report from another batch is not the same evidence. Kapiva states NABL reports are available per pack; we have not opened a specific report ourselves.

HealthKart describes it as a scratch-code authentication mechanism on eligible products. Check whether your exact product supports it and follow the instructions on the pack. We have not tested the mechanism.

items.q: Do I need to check veg/non-veg markers?
items.a: Yes. HK Vitals' collagen is non-vegetarian because it is fish-derived; the whey carries a vegetarian dot but contains milk and soy. Read the ingredient panel of the exact SKU before buying.

items.q: Did Durza test or consume these supplements?
items.a: No. We compared published label and retail data on 24 Nov 2026 and make no medical or efficacy claims. Consult a qualified professional before starting any supplement, especially if you are pregnant, under 18, or taking medication.
